name: Indian Island County Park
note: Suffolk County park at the Peconic River/Flanders Bay. ~100-150 tent & trailer sites, some electric; some water-view sites. --Claude  Verified 2026-09-14: the non-resident Green Key is $50 and valid one year, and without it the county reservation system cannot be used at all. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Suffolk County's online reservation system, with a Green Key login; on 2026-10-21 the county's Reservations page said a new reservation system is 'coming soon' and some services are temporarily unavailable. Reservations 1 to 180 days ahead (no same-day). From May 15 to Oct 15 a reservation must be at least 4 nights if it takes in Thursday-Sunday and 2 nights if Monday-Wednesday only; 2 nights the rest of the season. A reservation made with the $50 Non-Resident Reservation Green Key must be at least 4 nights at any time ('Non-Resident green key card holders may reserve throughout the season for one week maximum, except the following holiday weeks: Memorial Day ... Fourth of July ... Labor Day'). Sites not reserved go to walk-ups from 8 am, paid in full at check-in, at non-resident rates without a Green Key; the rig must be with you. At most 7 nights, then 7 nights away from that campground. Four people or one family (2 adults and their children) per site.
field_notes.Fees: Inherits the county row. Indian Island is NOT a Flagship Park, so the $4/night flagship surcharge does NOT apply here. One non-resident night in season, with electric: $36 base + $8 electric + site tier ($5 Tier II to $22 Premier) + $10 reservation + $3 registration, PLUS the $50 Non-Resident Reservation Green Key without which the booking cannot be made at all. On a single night the Green Key roughly doubles the trip cost; over a year of Long Island camping it is negligible. This is why prereq_pass is priced separately from the nightly rate.

name: Lake Placid Volunteer Fire Department Campground
note: Run by the Lake Placid Volunteer Fire Department (a nonprofit fire company) as a small RV lot by the fire station at 456 Old Military Rd; proceeds support the department; walk to downtown. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $40 a night in August 2026 (Campendium review); the fire department has no web page for the campground (2026-10-21). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Camper-reported: reservations by phone (518-390-0930) or online, paid by cash or check; replies are at volunteer pace. Campendium also gives lpvfdcampground@gmail.com.
field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED: $40 a night in an August 2026 Campendium review (also $40 in October 2025); the fire department posts no rate. Cash or check.

name: Sandhill RV Park & Camp
note: Local (McCreary County, Whitley City). 80 water+electric sites + primitive, dump station, showers, playground, shelter, community building. --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night in October 2024 (RV Life review); the park has no operator web page, and the county tourism listing gives no prices (2026-10-11). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: An RV Life reviewer paid $25 a night in October 2024. No operator rate page (McCreary County tourism lists the park without prices); confirm by phone.

name: Big Rock Campground
note: Local (Forest Preserve District of Kane County). 96 improved drive-in electric/water sites (handles 50-ft rigs), 2 dump stations, no showers; also tent + a few equestrian sites (general campground). Ponds/creek in preserve but not RV-site-adjacent. Seasonal May 1-mid Oct; reservations. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Forest Preserve District of Kane County: electric and water $26 a day for county residents, $41 non-residents; primitive $18/$24. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Loud Thunder Forest Preserve
note: Local (Rock Island County Forest Preserve District, Illinois City). RV camping in White Oak (26 water/electric sites) + Deer Haven (35 full-hookup 50A pull-throughs); showers, marina/boat rental on 167-acre Lake George, 12+ mi trails; separate equestrian loop. RV loops not on the water. Reservable, 2-night min, Apr-Oct. RV Life ~9/10. RV Life mislabels state; it is county FP. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Rock Island County Forest Preserve WebTrac fees: White Oak water/electric sites $24 for county residents and $27 for non-residents, Deer Haven full-hookup pull-throughs $27 / $30. Reserving is optional, but a reservation needs 2 nights.

name: Forest Glen Preserve
note: Local (Vermilion County Conservation District, Georgetown). Family campground: ~34 electric sites (20/30/50A, no water/sewer at site) + 8 non-electric, 2 dump stations. Separate Vermilion River canoe/backpack camp is not RV. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Vermilion County Conservation District (Forest Glen): sites with electricity $25 a day, non-electric $20. Read 2026-10-16.

name: Middle Fork Forest Preserve - Harry L. Swartz Campground
note: Local (Champaign County Forest Preserve District, Penfield). 65 sites (53 electric, 48 electric+water), on-site host, flush toilets/showers, summer swim beach, 11 dark-sky sites; small ponds not RV-site-adjacent. Reservations required. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Champaign County Forest Preserve District: $25 Sunday-Thursday, $30 Friday-Saturday, $40 holidays. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Arrow Rock State Historic Site
note: Wooded campground on the edge of the historic village, with a separate basic loop to the north. Big Soldier Lake is a 4-acre fishing pond beside the electric loops. Off-season (Nov 1-Mar 31) brings no water, showers or firewood. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: The park page's campground table gives reservations Apr 1-Oct 31 (camping year-round); 'Reservable sites may be available on a walk-up registration basis if the site is not reserved.' Online up to 12 months ahead or at 877-422-6766. Gates may be closed after 10 pm - arrive before then. 15 days in any 30.
field_notes.Fees: Park's own 2026 and 2027 rate sheets (identical, no weekend premium): on-season (Apr 1-Oct 31) basic $15, electric 30A $27, electric 50A $29, sewer/electric/water 50A $35; off-season (Nov 1-Mar 31) $14 / $23 / $25 / $29. Rates include sales tax. $6.50 online reservation fee per site.
field_notes.Sites: On the reservation system: 12 basic (36-51 ft, a separate loop to the north), 10 electric 30A (36-67 ft), 24 electric 50A (31-51 ft) and one sewer/electric/water 50A site (#43, 48 ft); every site takes a 23-ft rig. Campground host at site 48.

name: Bennett Spring State Park
note: Trout park with five campgrounds: #1 with full hookups beside the spring branch in the valley, open all year, and #2-#5 up a steep hill in the woods. Family sites hold two camping units. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Campground #1 (full hookups) is open year-round; #2 and #3 Apr 15-Oct 31, #4 and #5 Feb 25-Oct 31. Showers and water at #1 Apr 15-Oct 15.
field_notes.Booking: Every site in all five campgrounds, Campground 5 included, is on the reservation system (online up to 12 months ahead, or 877-422-6766); no minimum stay. Unreserved sites can be taken on a walk-up basis. Campgrounds 2-5 take reservations only in their own seasons. 15 days in any 30.
field_notes.Fees: Park's own 2026 and 2027 rate sheets (identical): on-season (Feb 25-Oct 31) basic $15, electric 30A $27, sewer/electric/water 50A $35, family/electric 30A $48; off-season (Nov 1-Feb 24) only the sewer/electric/water sites of Campground 1 are open, at $29. Rates include sales tax. $6.50 online reservation fee per site.
field_notes.Sites: Five campgrounds on the reservation system: #1 48 sewer/electric/water 50A (43-86 ft, beside the spring branch, open all year); #2 16 electric + 4 family-electric; #3 8 electric + 11 basic (two basic sites under 23 ft); #4 48 electric; #5 43 electric, 4 basic and 2 family. Campgrounds 2-5 are up a steep hill.

name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
note: Wooded campground in five loops north of the shut-ins day-use area: Loop 1 equestrian, Loop 2 full hookups, Loop 3 electric, Loop 4 basic and Loop 5 walk-in tent platforms, plus camper cabins. The shut-ins parking lot normally fills by 10 a.m. Memorial Day to Labor Day. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Showers and water Apr 1-Oct 31, except Loop 3 all year.
field_notes.Booking: Missouri State Parks' reservation site or 877-422-6766, up to 12 months ahead. 'The campground is fully reservable'; 'Reservable sites may be available on a walk-up registration basis if the site is not reserved.' The booking system here sets a 2-night minimum for Friday and Saturday arrivals in every season checked (January, April, June and October 2027; Sunday-Thursday arrivals 1 night) - not on the agency's list of seven two-night-weekend parks. Camping is limited to any 15 days within a 30-consecutive-day period.
field_notes.Fees: Park's own 2027 rate sheet (same as 2026): on-season (April-October) basic/walk-in $15, electric 50A $29, electric/water 50A $32, sewer/electric/water 50A $35; off-season (November-March) $14 / $25 / $26 / $29. Rates include sales tax. $6.50 online reservation fee per site.
field_notes.Sites: On the reservation system: Loop 1 equestrian electric/water 50A, 9 sites (56-92 ft; bookable by non-equestrian campers year-round); Loop 2 sewer/electric/water 50A, 19 (55-90 ft); Loop 3 electric 50A, 21 (54-85 ft); Loop 4 basic, 14 (53-70 ft); Loop 5 walk-in tent platforms, 14. Plus camper cabins and a special-use camping area.

name: Knob Noster State Park
note: Wooded campground on one long loop road; Lakes Buteo and Clearfork are nearby but not beside the sites. Sites 1-25 stay open all year; sites 26-60 close November 1-April 14. Generators are prohibited in the campground unless the park manager approves. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Online up to 12 months ahead or at 877-422-6766. Sites 1-25 are reservable year-round; sites 26-60 only April 15-October 31 (closed November 1-April 14). 'Reservable sites may be available on a walk-up registration basis if the site is not reserved.' No minimum stay on the grid. 15 days in any 30.
field_notes.Fees: Park's own 2026 and 2027 rate sheets (identical): on-season (April 15-October 31) basic $15, electric 30A $27, electric 50A $29, sewer/electric/water 50A $35, family basic $22, family electric 30A $42, family electric 50A $52; off-season (November 1-April 14) $14 / $23 / $25 / $29 / $20 / $36 / $46. Backcountry $10. Rates include sales tax; a family site (two pads) takes one reservation fee.
field_notes.Sites: 59 sites on the booking grid: 7 sewer/electric/water 50A, 34 electric 50A, 2 family electric 50A (F027, F031), 3 electric 30A, 13 basic. Pads 42-68 ft; every site fits 23 ft.

name: Pershing State Park
note: Small campground near the Locust Creek wetland with 26 30-amp electric and 12 basic sites; showers and water April 15 - October 31. Reservable online up to 12 months ahead; unreserved sites can be taken walk-up. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Missouri State Parks' reservation site or 877-422-6766, up to 12 months ahead. 'Reservable sites may be available on a walk-up registration basis if the site is not reserved.' Camping is limited to any 15 days within a 30-consecutive-day period. The booking system's restriction for this campground is a 1-night minimum, summer weekends included (checked June 11 and July 3, 2027).
field_notes.Fees: Missouri State Parks 2026 rates. On-season: basic $15, electric 30A $27. Off-season: basic $14, electric 30A $23. Charged by the site's utilities, used or not; $6.50 online reservation fee per site.
field_notes.Sites: 38 campsites on the reservation system: 26 electric 30-amp (listed vehicle lengths 36-63 ft) and 12 basic (23-85 ft), plus a special-use camping area.

name: Roaring River State Park
note: Three campgrounds in the Roaring River valley near Cassville, about 1.3 km apart. The spring-fed river here is a stream about 15-25 m wide; Campground 2's sites 093-094 at the end of its loop sit on the bank, and the lower Campground 1 sites (070-072) are a short walk through woods from it. Campground 1 stays open year-round with its showerhouse and frost-free water. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Campground #1 is open year-round, with showers and water; #2 and #3 Feb 25-Oct 31.
field_notes.Booking: Campground 1 takes reservations year-round; Campgrounds 2 and 3 Feb 25-Oct 31.
field_notes.Fees: Park's own 2026 and 2027 rate sheets (identical): on-season (February 25-October 31) basic $16, electric 30A $28, electric 50A $30, sewer/electric/water 50A $36, family basic $29, family electric 30A $49 / 50A $53; off-season (November 1-February 24) $15 / $24 / $26 / $30 / $27 / $43 / $47. Water at the sewer/electric/water sites depends on the weather. Rates include sales tax; a family site (two pads) takes one reservation fee.
field_notes.Sites: 169 campsites on the booking grid: Campground 1 68 (44 electric 30A, 16 electric 50A, 8 family electric), Campground 2 36 (29 electric 30A, 6 electric 50A, 1 family electric), Campground 3 65 (11 basic, 1 family basic, 19 electric 30A, 2 electric 50A, 1 family electric, 31 sewer/electric/water 50A). Pads 41-80 ft; every site fits 23 ft.

name: Wallace State Park
note: Four wooded campgrounds near Cameron, south of small Lake Allaman. Campgrounds 1 and 2 stay open all year; 3 and 4 close November to mid-April. The booking site lists every basic pad at 20 ft; the electric pads run 38-99 ft. Park gates close at 9 p.m. in season and at sunset off-season. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'For weekend reservations, there is a required two-night minimum stay of Friday/Saturday or Saturday/Sunday.'
field_notes.Fees: Park's 2027 rate sheet: on-season (April 15-October 31) / off-season (November 1-April 14) basic or walk-in $15 / $14, electric 30A $27 / $23, electric 50A $29 / $25. Rates include sales tax.
field_notes.Sites: 81 campsites on the booking grid: Campground 1 (30 basic, 4 tent-only walk-in), Campground 2 (22 electric 30A), Campground 3 (5 basic), Campground 4 (18 electric 30A, 2 electric 50A). Electric pads 38-99 ft (one at 20); every basic pad is listed at 20 ft. 19 pull-throughs.

name: Mozingo Lake Recreation Park
note: City of Maryville park on the roughly 1,000-acre Mozingo Lake, with three RV campgrounds: South (95 sites, on a peninsula), North (20 concrete sites) and a riders' equestrian campground on the west shore. 40 South and North sites are reservable online for up to 14 days; the rest are first come, first served and may stay longer at staff discretion. The South campground and its shower house stay open all winter; the North and Equestrian close from November 1 to March 1. --Claude

field_notes.Season: The South campground stays open all winter; the North and Equestrian close from November 1 to March 1.
field_notes.Booking: Reservable sites take stays of up to 14 days; first-come sites allow longer.
field_notes.Fees: Water and electric $32 a night in peak season (April 1-October 31), $28 off season (November 1-March 31); full hookups $38 / $32. The 13-site equestrian campground, dedicated to riders, is $28 / $25. Every reservable RV site carries a $10 booking fee; CampLife's estimate for a full-hookup site is $48 a night ($38 + $10). The water-and-electric sites (116-175) are first come, first served.
field_notes.Sites: 115 RV sites open to any camper: South 95 (101-115 and 176-195 full hookups, 116-175 water and electric) and North 20 (201-220, 30/50A), with 20 more North sites due for reservations in 2027; the 13-site equestrian campground (301-313) is dedicated to riders. The 40 reservable non-equestrian sites are 35-50 ft on CampLife; the operator gives 20-50 ft for the whole park, and the first-come pads on imagery run about 15-20 m.

name: Campus RV Park
note: On the old Swope Mansion grounds in historic downtown Independence, half a mile from the Truman Home; concrete pads, with full-hookup and electric-only sites. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Read on CampLife: one night, site rate before tax, every RV site a 23-ft rig fits (Electric Only, Patio, Back In and Pull Through). October 2026: $35-51.64 on a Tuesday. January 2027: $51.64, Tuesday and Saturday alike. June 2027: $35-51.64, Tuesday and Saturday alike. Read 2026-10-14. Tax brings a full-hookup night to $55.00 ($51.64 plus $3.36), the starting rate the park's own site advertises.

name: B Berry Farms & Co.
note: U-pick berry farm with five electric RV spots at the front, among tent sites; water spigot about 15 ft from the RV sites, gray-water dump only ($10). Farm play park and splash area for a per-person fee. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Instant book on Hipcamp, one-night minimum; some spots by phone only. Online booking runs to 8 pm on arrival day, then call or text. Check-in 1 pm, check-out noon. Extended stays Nov 1-Mar 1.
field_notes.Fees: Hipcamp host prices: 'Pullin On Over' (a plain pull-over spot at the front, to 60 ft) $8, electric extra; 'RV There Yet' $20 with 30A (50A extra); 'RV Pop'n' pull-through $25 with 30A. Hipcamp adds a $3-4.44 service fee. The farm's own page quotes higher, undated: RV sites $25-26, 50A $29. Gray-water dump $10. No refunds.
field_notes.Sites: 16 Hipcamp sites (tent, RV/tent and a bunkhouse), of which five are electric RV spots at the front of the farm; RV limits per site 20-60 ft.

name: Majestic Oaks Park
note: Wooded campground on 44 acres of oaks a few minutes from Bagnell Dam, with gravel, shaded sites, a swimming pool (mid-May to mid-September), nature trails, a dog park and a bike pump track. Seasonal and monthly sites are sold besides the nightly ones. --Claude

field_notes.Season: A very few full-hookup RV sites are kept for winter stays from November 1 to March 31, by phone.
field_notes.Booking: Check-in and checkout at noon. A specific site can be 'locked in' for $10; otherwise the park assigns a site that fits the rig's length and amperage. Cancelling more than two weeks out costs $25, two weeks to 48 hours $50, under 48 hours no refund. Cabins, glamping tents and the rental camper take 2 nights; RV sites showed no minimum.
field_notes.Fees: The park's campsites page gives RV sites at $44-64 a night and tent sites at $28-37, the tent sites including overflow RV sites with water and electric. Campspot sells four of those, 'Tent or RV 20/30 W/E' (sites A-D, 25-34 ft, motorhomes allowed on A, C and D), at $32 a night before tax; its full-hookup types run $44 (standard back-in 30A) to $59 (deluxe pull-through). Campspot adds the park's $6 reservation fee per stay and a 3.5% processing fee.
field_notes.Sites: Campspot sells 33 RV sites (25-47 ft) and 15 tent sites; the FAQ counts 28 full-hookup sites for nightly rental. Seasonal and monthly sites are kept besides.

name: Perry State Park
note: KDWP state park on the southwest shore of Perry Reservoir, 4 mi north of US-24 on K-237. The reservable hookup loops are Lakeview (pinned: 50 A, mostly pull-through, beside the swim-beach lot and cabins) with Cougar Pass and Cottonwood Bridge just south and Eagle Landing about 1 km north; Hobie Cove primitive, more first-come sites, and the horse-only Wild Horse equestrian campground are elsewhere in the park. The Hobie Cove shower house is permanently closed. --Claude

Booking: min stay 3 nights on holidays (Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule))

field_notes.Booking: The hookup loops (Lakeview, Cougar Pass, Cottonwood Bridge, Eagle Landing) reserve site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); unreserved sites allow self-registration on arrival, and KDWP lists further first-come primitive and water/electric sites. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park. Wild Horse is for campers with horses only.
field_notes.Fees: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or $15 for three (full hookups), and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site this campground has, per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Fall River State Park (Quarry Bay)
note: Fall River SP's primitive campground on the lake side at the north-east end of the dam, across the lake from the Fredonia Bay hookup sites. No hookups: all 17 sites are primitive and booked as tent sites; the gravel back-ins 407-417 list 24-50 ft vehicle lengths (2026-11-06). --Claude

Booking: min stay 3 nights on holidays (Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule))

field_notes.Booking: Primitive sites reserved site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); self-registration is also allowed. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights; a 14-day extension needs the park manager's written permission, and a five-day absence is required before camping again.
field_notes.Fees: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or $15 for three (full hookups), and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site this campground has, per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.
field_notes.Sites: 17 primitive sites: 11 gravel back-ins (407-417, 24-50 ft) and six 15-ft asphalt pads (401-406). The booking site labels all of them 'Tent Site'.

name: Prairie Dog State Park
note: On Keith Sebelius Reservoir near Norton; ~80 W/E (incl 10 full-hookup, 13 electric-only) + ~154 primitive across Prairie Dog, Shady Rest, Cedar Ridge, Cottonwood and Meadowlark loops (travelks; ReserveAmerica). Reservable online. --Claude

Booking: min stay 4 nights on holidays (Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends), 3 on holidays (July 4th weekend)

field_notes.Season: ReserveAmerica: campsites reservable April 1 - October 31, certain sites open through December 31; facility status 'Open year round'. Water is shut off from about mid-October to mid-April.
field_notes.Booking: ReserveAmerica: 'Campsites are reservable April 1-Oct 31. Certain sites may be open through Dec. 31 of the current year. Reservations for the following year will open in mid-December.' 2026 holiday minimums: Memorial Day weekend 4 nights, July 4th weekend 3 nights, Labor Day weekend 4 nights (each Thursday or Friday start). Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground; a one-time 14-day extension needs the park manager's written permission, and a five-day absence is required before camping again.
field_notes.Fees: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or $15 for three (full hookups), and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site this campground has, per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.
field_notes.Sites: ReserveAmerica lists 238 campsites: 147 primitive, 79 water and electric, 10 full hookup and 2 electric-only, across Prairie Dog, Shady Rest, Cedar Ridge, Branded Cedar, Cottonwood and Meadowlark areas (plus 4 cabins). The park's description says 69 electric/water, 12 electric-only and more than 130 primitive sites. Cedar Ridge and Branded Cedar sites sampled are pull-through, listed to 80 ft.

name: Glen Elder State Park
note: KDWP park on the north shore of 12,500-acre Waconda Lake (Glen Elder Reservoir). Reservable water/electric sites, mostly 50-amp, in four campgrounds: Kanza (66, the largest, by the marina cove), Kiowa (20, just north of Kanza), Cheyenne (36, 0.8 km east) and Kaw (18, 1 km west), on concrete, asphalt or gravel pads; primitive camping in Kanza and Cheyenne and in several unreserved areas (Osage, Sioux, Pawnee). Shower houses at Kanza, Cheyenne and Kaw; full-service marina; two rental cabins. --Claude

Booking: min stay 3 nights on holidays (Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule))

field_notes.Season: Concrete sites south of the Kanza shower building and Cheyenne's concrete pads stay open in winter, first come first served; the other utility campgrounds and shower houses close from late fall until April 15 (Kanza's showers until November 19).
field_notes.Booking: The 140 water/electric sites in Kanza, Kiowa, Cheyenne and Kaw reserve site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); unreserved sites allow self-registration on arrival, and the primitive areas (Osage, Sioux, Pawnee and others) take no reservations. In winter only the Kanza and Cheyenne concrete sites are open, first come first served. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park.
field_notes.Fees: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or $15 for three (full hookups), and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site this campground has, per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Lovewell State Park
note: KDWP state park on the north shore of Bureau of Reclamation Lovewell Reservoir (RV Life mislabels it commercial 'Lovewell Lake'): Willow, Cottonwood, Cedar Point and Walleye Point campgrounds with electric, water/electric and full-hookup sites plus primitive areas, camping cabins and yurts; full-service marina April-September; the dense Twin Coves trailer rows are leased spaces, not transient sites. Pinned at Willow, the first-come utility campground. --Claude

Booking: min stay 3 nights on holidays (Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule))

field_notes.Booking: Cedar Point, Cottonwood and Walleye Point electric sites reserve site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); Willow's sites and the primitive areas are first come, first served. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park.
field_notes.Fees: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or $15 for three (full hookups), and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site this campground has, per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Hillsdale State Park
note: West-shore campgrounds in two groups: Sunflower and Scott Creek by the entrance road, and the Russell Crites loops (Pintail Point, Crappie Cove, Quail Run) ~1.6 km north on the points, where the lake-edge sites are. Rabbit Ridge is primitive. Showerhouses in season (Apr 15-Oct 15 per park brochure). Saddle Ridge, on the east side, is the equestrian camp. --Claude

Booking: min stay 3 nights on holidays (Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule))

field_notes.Booking: Reserved site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov). 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground; to stay longer a guest must move to a different campground within the park. Rabbit Ridge's primitive sites are not reservable (KDWP).
field_notes.Fees: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or $15 for three (full hookups), and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site this campground has, per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.
field_notes.Sites: 219 utility sites in the west-shore campgrounds: Sunflower 61 and Scott Creek 60 by the entrance road, and the Russell Crites loops ~1.6 km north (Pintail Point 42, Crappie Cove 37, Quail Run 19). Gravel or concrete pads, mostly back-ins 30-90 ft, with a few pull-throughs. Plus primitive sites (Rabbit Ridge 42, Russell Crites 21) and the Saddle Ridge equestrian camp (22 W/E, 12 primitive) on the east side. A lone 110-ft back-in (Sunflower 120) is left out of the maximum.

name: Milford State Park
note: On the southeast shore of Milford Reservoir, Kansas's largest lake. The campgrounds sit in two clusters about 2 km apart on the park road: Woodland Hills (the pin), Hickory Hollow, Walnut Grove and Cedar Point (a marina peninsula whose west-row sites sit just above the water) to the north; Eagle Ridge, Prairie View (on a cove), Sunset Ridge and Rusty Windmill to the south. Cabins and equestrian camping too. --Claude

Booking: min stay 3 nights on holidays (Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule))

field_notes.Booking: Cedar Point, Eagle Ridge, Hickory Hollow, Woodland Hills, Walnut Grove and Sunset Ridge reserve site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov); KDWP lists Prairie View and Rusty Windmill as not reservable (campitks still lists their sites), so those are first come, first served. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park. 31 sites are marked long-term.
field_notes.Fees: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus utilities at $11 a night for one (electric), $13 for two (water and electric) or $15 for three (full hookups), and $2 a night more for a designated prime site April-September. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. The add-ons listed are the kinds of site this campground has, per KDWP's park page; water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.
field_notes.Sites: Utility sites run 30-75 ft (Eagle Ridge all 75 ft; Cedar Point asphalt pads 40-74 ft); the 98-ft sites are primitive (Woodland Hills, Walnut Grove). Pull-throughs at Woodland Hills, Hickory Hollow, Prairie View, Sunset Ridge, Cedar Point and Walnut Grove.
